overview: This bill, the Stop Child Care Fraud Act, adds to what states must include in the plans they submit to receive money from the Child Care and Development Block Grant program, the main federal program that gives states money to help low-income families pay for child care. Each state plan would have to describe the state's internal controls to keep the program accountable, its processes for investigating and recovering fraudulent payments and penalizing families or providers who commit fraud, and its procedures for checking that families are eligible. States would also have to explain how they use data from other state and local agencies that oversee child care providers. As of April 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say requiring states to spell out their anti-fraud safeguards up front encourages stronger controls and makes it easier to see which states fall short.
against: Critics say the bill adds planning paperwork without new resources, and that describing safeguards on paper does not guarantee they work in practice.
